title: Semantic vector sanity lab notes
content:
Purpose:
This is an internal lab-style playbook for constructing compact evaluation sets and quick smoke suites for semantic vector quality across three axes: semantic search relevance, clustering sanity, and multilingual stability. Goal is a lightweight nightly/regression-friendly set we can run locally and in CI to catch major regressions when onboarding new embedding models or quantization pipelines.

Scope and constraints:
- Focus: sentence/document embeddings used in semantic search and k-NN based clustering for product search, help center, and small-scale multilingual retrieval.
- Not exhaustive: this is intentionally small (approx 1k vectors total) to be fast in CI. Larger evals live in the embed-eval corpus.
- Designed to surface large, actionable diffs (precision/recall shifts, cluster collapse, language-specific drifts).
- Contains synthetic and real text mixes: curated queries, paraphrase clusters, near-duplicate noise, and non-English clusters.

Dataset composition (high level):
- English relevance pairs: 300 query-candidate pairs from help center + internal KB (annotated R1..R3 relevances).
- Paraphrase clusters: 120 clusters (3-5 sentences each) across intent types (search, command, FAQ).
- Near-duplicate noise bank: 150 pairs with small lexical differences (typos, punctuation, template variables).
- Multilingual anchors: 200 sentence anchors across 6 languages (es, fr, de, pt, ja, zh), each with 2-3 translations + distractors.
- Hard negatives: 150 engineered negatives (domain-matched but semantically different).
- Holding set: 80 examples reserved for seed-level regression checks (do not modify without version bump).

Annotation schema and labeling notes:
- Relevance labels: 0 (irrelevant), 1 (related), 2 (relevant), 3 (highly relevant). Use conservative labeling: if annotator unsure pick lower bin and comment.
- Cluster labels: cluster_id strings and cluster_intent tags (e.g., account-billing, troubleshooting, product-feature).
- Language tag: ISO 639-1 codes.
- Annotator comments: short free text for failure explanation (format: "[ticket-suggestion] short note").
- Inter-annotator checks: 10% overlap, compute Cohen's kappa; target >= 0.7 for relevance.

Evaluation measures (CI / nightly):
- Retrieval: Recall@1/5/10, MRR, nDCG@10.
- Ranking drift detection: KL on score distribution across seeds.
- Clustering sanity: silhouette score, adjusted rand index (ARI) vs labels, cluster purity@k.
- Multilingual stability: per-language Recall@5 and delta vs English baseline.
- Robustness probes: cosine drop on near-duplicates, percent of pairs with cosine < 0.6 for identical paraphrases.

Acceptance criteria (quick guards):
- Recall@5 for core help-center queries must not drop >3 percentage points vs baseline model (baseline = model-v3/float16).
- Global MRR drop >5% -> immediate block and triage.
- Any language with >6pt drop in Recall@5 flagged.
- Silhouette collapse >0.1 absolute drop requires investigation.

Test harness & CI integration:
- Use vector-eval-runner (python script) to produce a compact JSON report and histogram artifacts.
- Nightly workflow: run full suite on a short queue (GPU not required) and upload results to S3 prefix: s3://redwood-evals/semantic-vector-sanity/{model}/{date}/report.json.
- Slack alerting: post to #eng-applied-ml on blocked thresholds (see acceptance criteria).
- Tags: each run records model-id, tokenization/quantization tags, shuffle seed, and KNN index type (faiss-flat / faiss-IVF / hnsw).

Quick run (local):
- python -m vector_eval.runner --suite semantic-sanity --model path_or_id --output ./tmp/report.json
- Notebook: notebooks/semantic_vector_quicklook.ipynb (coverage: embedding hist, recall curves, t-SNE snapshots).

Multilingual considerations and pitfalls:
- Crosslingual anchor selection: prefer natural parallel pairs rather than machine-translated ones if available. MT introduces correlated errors that mask model drift.
- Tokenization mismatch: watch for models that implicitly lower-case vs cased training; we include lowercase and original variants for 25% of non-English anchors.
- Script variance: zh/ja examples include mixed-script tokens (Latin punctuation) to catch brittle pre-tokenizers.
- Locale-specific stopwords: do not remove stopwords during sampling — they can be important signals for short queries.

Cluster sanity checks (practical heuristics):
- Query: sample 50 clusters, compute top-3 nearest neighbors for each cluster centroid and verify majority label presence.
- Collapse detection: if >30% of clusters have centroid pairwise cosine > 0.92 (too close), likely over-compression/quantization side effect.
- Noise-robustness: inject 10% synthetic template tokens ({{user}}) and measure rank movement; >15% movement for core intents is red flag.

Known failure modes (from prior runs):
- Quantized 8-bit kernels caused underflow for short sequences -> paraphrase separation reduced (MRR down ~7%).
- Recent tokenizer tweak (strip punctuation) introduced English recall regression for short queries (<5 tokens).
- Small-capacity models collapse multilingual embeddings towards English for languages with few tokens.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we add voice-to-text transcripts (ASR noise) to the near-duplicate bank? (impacts customer support product). TODO: run 50 sample queries via ASR.
- Evaluate effect of per-language whitening vs global whitening on clustering metrics. Assigned: Chen Wei.
- Explore metric thresholding for silhouette vs ARI — which correlates more with downstream rerank A/B? Liam to prototype.

Versioning & maintenance rules:
- Any change to the holding set or core acceptance criteria must include a short changelog entry in CHANGES.md and a corresponding Jira task.
- Add a model-badlist.json to lock examples known to be flaky (e.g., legal templates) to avoid noisy alerts.

Appendix: quick annotation checklist for labelers:
- Read full example pair before labeling.
- Mark language and cluster intent first.
- Use 'related' (1) if candidate contains partial but actionable information.
- Leave short comment when marking 0 for near-duplicates.

Notes to self (working):
- Prioritize adding 50 new help-center queries from November releases.
- Merge with crosslingual-anchor-probe next sprint.
- Follow up with SRE to ensure CI job has 2-hour timeout and retry policy.
